description: We are a team of student siblings who are interested in pursuing engineering (Nitro) and computer science (Kepler).
summary:
HealthTree is a user-intuitive app that allows astronauts easy diagnosis for possible health issues. We addressed the challenge in an easy to use, user intuitive format. By abstracting unnecessary jargon in the concepts, we allow astronauts to easily navigate possible issues and treatments without needing a medicine-heavy background. At the core of our mission is the user, not the program. Instead of overwhelming users with large amounts of information, we simply display the information relevant to them, so they can administer treatments more effectively. 
HealthTree also sports a dual-report system. HealthTree continuously monitors the vitals of the astronauts and their environments, which allows it to flag a possible health abnormality. When a health abnormality is flagged, the astronauts are alerted, and the astronaut (or their companions) is prompted to conduct a manual report. Users also have the option to conduct a manual report directly without anything being flagged.
details:
What does it do / How does it work:

- Our project works through a user-based report system (for when a user experiences health abnormalities or when they notice such occurrences in their teammates), with two main modes: Manual (User) and Semi-automatic (System Flags). When the system flags a health abnormality, the system prompts the astronauts to enter a manual report regarding the team member who has sustained said abnormality.

What is the intended impact of the project:

- HealthTree is intended to serve as a user-friendly medical guide. When people are struggling to see, especially with some of the possible space ailments causing difficulty focusing. By abstracting and simplifying the program, we allow those in need to easily and efficiently access the information they require without needing prior medical knowledge.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

- We utilized the following software, tools, and coding languages: VS Code, Github, GitHub Desktop, Python, Streamlit (Python Library), Coolors.Co (Color palette), Google Fonts, Google Docs (Brainstorming), Gemini (Debugging), Copilot (Debugging), Claude (Debugging, Code Generation, Data Analysis, Small Chunks of Text).

How is your project creative?

- Our project is creative because of the user friendly nature. By prioritizing user experience, we've deliberately simplified our application. We've chosen a forest inspired color scheme to contrast the mechanical interior of spacecrafts and we've tested our color palette to ensure that the colorblind could easily access information through our application.

What factors did your team consider?

- We considered factors such as Colorblindness, Medical Inexperience, Possible issues sustained by crew members that could impede their usage of the app, and differing personal healthy baselines.
